messages:
maria: Quick sync  we need a short decision: accept quantized model binaries into the registry as first-class artifacts?
ben: Clarify format: .pt q4/q8 artifacts that teams produce locally?
maria: Exactly. Goal is to let teams upload quantized checkpoints and have them go through onboarding (smoke + bench) without forcing a float-only policy.
jordan: Upside: cheaper/easier perf testing on Dedicated/private infra. Downside: quantization can mask correctness regressions vs fp32.
ali: Suggested boundary: accept quantized upload, but require a deterministic parity check in the bench. e.g., run 100 seeded golden prompts and compute a quality delta metric; block if below threshold.
ben: Parity runs are tricky because of nondeterminism across kernels. For parity we need deterministic seeds, pinned kernels (or CPU fallback), and a defined sampling mode (greedy/topk).
maria: Operational proposal: require two pieces on upload: (1) quantized artifact, (2) a minimal float baseline (can be a trimmed fp32 snapshot). Validation: immediate smoke (sanity + latency), plus async parity-run. If parity fails, block promotion to higher trust levels.
jordan: How tight are parity thresholds? Exact token equality improbable. Start with n-gram overlap (e.g., BLEU-style) + targeted hallucination checks (does answer mention spurious facts).
ali: Also require metadata headers describing quantization recipe + tooling version (e.g., bitsandbytes v0.40, per-channel clamp flags). This helps explain diffs.
ben: Storage concerns: storing a second baseline increases registry size. Options: allow baseline as compressed tar or external URL (must be accessible to validator). For private/offline installs, baseline must be included in package.
maria: Registry behavior: if baseline provided as URL, fetch it during validation; if large (>500MB) async validate and notify uploader when finished. (sre-bot note).
sre-bot: deploybot: FYI  uploads >500MB trigger async validation; uploader gets email when done.
jordan: Fallback: if quantized passes smoke but fails parity, allow "dev"-level soft-approve for internal testing but block "approved" trust for Dedicated/public rollouts.
ali: Add registry field quant_trust_level with values [dev, internal, approved], default dev. This is surfaced in the Console and gated for routing.
ben: Bench output should include a quality_delta column with parity score, quant-recipe tag, and link to baseline commit. Optimize will consume that.
maria: Action items: I'll write a short follow-up doc covering required metadata, parity test spec (100 seeded cases, scoring function, deterministic config), trust levels, and storage options. @ben please sketch an example metadata schema; @jordan propose an initial scoring threshold (maybe ~0.85 n-gram overlap + perplexity delta cap).
ben: Example metadata snippet (in doc):
```
quant.meta = {
  "q_bits": "4",
  "tool": "bitsandbytes",
  "tool_version": "0.40",
  "recipe": "perchannel-clamp",
  "baseline_url": "s3://redwood-registry/baselines/llama-2-7b-fp32.tar.gz",
  "trust_level": "dev"
}
```
jordan: I'll prototype the scorer next week: combine n-gram overlap (primary) with perplexity delta and a hallucination binary check. Start conservative, iterate.
ali: If anyones OOO, ping me  I'll consolidate comments into the RFC follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks. Landing doc by Fri EOD. If you want to bike-shed metrics, discuss in the doc thread.
ben: ack
jordan: ack
ali: ack
